weather.tip: A 96% chance of rain today means it's a near-certainty — carry an umbrella and budget extra travel time on waterlogging-prone stretches like Varthur and Gunjur, which are already jammed this week.

around.headline: Two separate domestic-violence killings of women reported in Bengaluru
around.summary: Police are investigating after a man allegedly strangled his partner following an argument, and separately a Bihar man was held for killing his wife, per The Indian Express and The Times of India. If you or someone you know is at risk, Karnataka's women's helpline (181) takes calls for early intervention, not just emergencies.
around.source: The Indian Express, The Times of India

around.headline: Varthur-Gunjur school-commute gridlock stretches into a third day
around.summary: Exam-bound children are still taking over two hours to cover just a few kilometres in East Bengaluru traffic, per The Times of India and NDTV. If your route runs through Varthur, Gunjur or Whitefield, keep building in a large buffer until this eases.

around.headline: BMRCL to add 21 new Namma Metro trains by 2027
around.summary: The expansion is meant to ease overcrowding on existing lines even as the Phase 3 double-decker project faces delays, per Inshorts. Worth checking off-peak metro timings now if crowding is a factor in your commute.

around.headline: Centre working on a system to keep UPI transaction fees off customers
around.summary: The government is preparing a mechanism so that any UPI processing costs are absorbed rather than passed on to users, per Hindustan Times. No action needed for now — just a reason not to worry if you hear talk of UPI charges.

around.headline: Trump signs Russia sanctions bill into law as oil futures fall for a third day
around.summary: The new US sanctions target Russia's oil trade, while crude prices have been easing on supply concerns, per The Hindu and WSJ. Softer global crude can eventually feed into local petrol and diesel prices, though effects usually lag by weeks.

street_smart.title: You book a cab through a ride-hailing app for a fixed quoted fare. When you get in, the driver says the app price 'doesn't apply right now' because of traffic, and insists you pay him nearly double, in cash, before he'll start the trip. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Deccan Herald, Sept 19 — a report examining who actually sets cab fares, the meter or the app, points directly at this everyday dispute: drivers claiming the app fare doesn't apply and demanding a higher cash amount instead. Auto/cab overcharging hasn't been used as a street-smart scenario in the last three weeks.
street_smart.situation: You're already running late, the driver isn't being aggressive about it, and he's framing it as normal practice rather than a scam — which makes it tempting to just pay and move on.

choices.text: Pay the cash amount he's asking so you can get going without a scene.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. It rewards the exact behaviour that's meant to pressure you, leaves no record of what actually happened, and does nothing to stop the same demand being made of the next passenger.

choices.text: Refuse to pay above the app-quoted fare, screenshot the fare estimate and trip details, and end or report the ride through the app's help section with the driver ID and vehicle number.
choices.feedback: Correct. Screenshots and the driver/vehicle ID are exactly what the app's grievance system needs to investigate and refund an overcharge — it's the fastest route that actually holds the driver accountable, not just you.

choices.text: Get out of the cab immediately without paying anything and walk off.
choices.feedback: Risky. It can leave you stranded and settles nothing for the next rider, since there's no formal complaint or record of the attempted overcharge.

choices.text: Argue with the driver in person until he backs down and agrees to the original fare.
choices.feedback: Risky — it might work, but it can also escalate into a confrontation with no record to fall back on if things turn unpleasant, especially if you're travelling alone.

takeaways: Screenshot the app's fare estimate before the ride starts — it's your main evidence if the driver later disputes the price.
Report overcharging through the app's own help or 'fare issue' flow rather than just arguing in person; it triggers an actual review and possible refund.
Note the vehicle number if a driver refuses the meter/app fare or turns aggressive — you can also escalate to the Bengaluru Traffic Police helpline (1512).

quiz.question: How many new Namma Metro trains is BMRCL planning to add by 2027, per today's reports?
quiz.why: The addition is meant to ease overcrowding on existing lines even as the separate Phase 3 double-decker corridor faces delays.

quiz.question: President Trump signed a bill today imposing new sanctions tied to which country's oil trade?
quiz.why: Such sanctions often also target buyers of that country's oil, which is part of why India's own oil-import choices get scrutinised in these moments.

quiz.question: According to today's report, what is the Indian government working to ensure about UPI transactions?
options: That a new fee is introduced
That any processing fee doesn't get passed on to customers
That daily UPI limits are cut to ₹1,000
quiz.why: UPI transactions for individuals have been fee-free (zero MDR) for years; this move is about keeping any backend processing costs from trickling down to users.

quiz.question: Under India's Juvenile Justice Act, what is the general age below which a person is treated as a juvenile?
quiz.why: 16-to-18-year-olds can still be tried as adults, but only for heinous crimes and only after a case-by-case assessment by a Juvenile Justice Board.

quiz.question: Which gas makes up the largest share of Earth's atmosphere by volume?
quiz.why: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of the atmosphere, with oxygen a distant second at roughly 21%.
